extraction.name: Data Recipes for Reasoning Models
extraction.description: Paper describing the OpenThoughts project and the construction of OpenThoughts3-1.2M, an open-source reasoning dataset for math, code, and science, along with OpenThinker3-7B models trained on it.
extraction.creator: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, Hritik Bansal, Marianna Nezhurina, Jean Mercat, Trung Vu, Zayne Sprague, Ashima Suvama, Benjamin Feuer, Liangyu Chen, Zaid Khan, Eric Frankel, Sachin Grover, Caroline Choi, Niklas Muennighoff, Shiye Su, Wanjia Zhao, John Yang, Shreyas Pimpalgaonkar, Kartik Sharma, Charlie Cheng-Jie Ji, Yichuan Deng, Sarah Pratt, Vivek Ramanujan, Jon Saad-Falcon, Jeffrey Li, Achal Dave, Alon Albalak, Kushal Arora, Blake Wulfe, Chinmay Hegde, Greg Durrett, Sewoong Oh, Mohit Bansal, Saadia Gabriel, Aditya Grover, Kai-Wei Chang, Vaishaal Shankar, Aaron Gokaslan, Mike A. Merrill, Tatsunori Hashimoto, Yejin Choi, Jenia Jitsev, Reinhard Heckel, Maheswaran Sathiamoorthy, Alexandros G. Dimakis, Ludwig Schmidt
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The OpenThoughts project builds reasoning datasets by sourcing questions from existing datasets and forums, generating new questions with LLMs, generating answers with teacher models, filtering questions and answers, deduplicating questions, and selecting multiple answers per question. The paper reports more than 1,000 controlled experiments over the pipeline and then scales the final recipe to OpenThoughts3-1.2M.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper explicitly notes that some source datasets contain unverified samples and that answer filtering was not beneficial overall, but it does not provide a general missing-data description for the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions and text were sourced from public forums, competition sites, textbooks, pretraining corpora, and existing datasets such as StackExchange CodeGolf, OpenCodeReasoning, OpenMath-2-Math, NuminaMath, StackExchange Physics, Organic Chemistry PDF sources, CodeForces, LiveCodeBench, GPQA Diamond, JEEBench, and others listed in the appendix.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Not explicitly stated for the dataset collection process; the paper states the paper was posted on 5 Jun 2025 and references source datasets and accesses up to 2025-05-11 in citations.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were filtered, mixed, deduplicated, and in some cases repeated to reach target counts; answers were generated by teacher models; some sources were refined or extracted from PDFs; decontamination removed samples similar to evaluation benchmarks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The pipeline includes filtering questions by difficulty or response length, deduplicating questions using exact or fuzzy string similarity, sampling multiple answers per question, optionally filtering answers, and decontaminating against evaluation sets using Indel similarity and n-gram overlap. For some sources, questions were repeated to reach the desired number of datapoints.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations consist of teacher-generated reasoning traces and answers, plus human/LLM-based filtering labels such as difficulty ratings, verification judgments, and majority-consensus selection. The final dataset uses teacher model outputs rather than manual labels for most examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: LlamaFactory was used for training; Evalchemy was used for evaluation; GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1-nano, DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B, and Phi-4-reasoning-plus were used in annotation/filtering workflows; FastText and OpenAI embeddings were used for filtering.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper analyzes annotation choices via ablations, including majority consensus, GPT verification, difficulty ratings, response-length selection, and comparisons between teachers. It reports that stronger teachers are not always better teachers, and that verification often did not improve performance.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 16 answers per question in the final pipeline; some ablations also use 1x, 4x, and 16x sampling, and some experiments use 5x annotation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Not applicable; annotators are models and no human annotator demographics are reported.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1-nano, DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B, Phi-4-reasoning-plus, Claude 3.7, Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite, FastText, OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, Math-Verify, Evalchemy, LlamaFactory
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states that all datasets and models are available on openthoughts.ai and also released on Hugging Face and GitHub, but it does not specify a versioning, update schedule, maintainer policy, or deprecation policy.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal sensitive information is described as being collected as part of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses broader impacts on reasoning-model development and notes safety trade-offs: supervised fine-tuning on reasoning can degrade safety alignment and increase harmfulness, highlighting the need to balance utility and safety.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper suggests potential biases from source selection and cross-domain transfer, and notes that limited question diversity may have relatively little impact when answer diversity is high. It also reports that some source choices and teacher choices perform better than others, indicating dataset-source bias.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper states several limitations: it did not explore reinforcement-learning datasets, staged SFT, or curriculum learning; it optimized strategies for overall average benchmark performance rather than per-domain performance; and it notes open questions about scaling, cross-domain transfer, and question/answer diversity. It also reports that distilled reasoning models still show generalization deficits on simple perturbation tests.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and fine-tuning reasoning models; the datasets are used for supervised fine-tuning and evaluation of reasoning models across math, code, and science benchmarks.
